questions.stem: Who coined the modern definition of the term business intelligence, and in which year?
options: Edgar Codd in 1970
Bill Inmon in 1992
Ralph Kimball in 1996
Howard Dresner in 1989
Peter Drucker in 1954
questions.explanation: Howard Dresner coined the modern definition of business intelligence in 1989, in the sense typically used in industry today.

questions.stem: What is the modern definition of business intelligence attributed to Howard Dresner?
options: End-user access to and analysis of structured content, that is, data
Automated forecasting of future KPIs
The manual effort of financial consultants
A repository for unstructured social media data
A machine learning model that runs itself
questions.explanation: Dresner's definition is end-user access to and analysis of structured content, that is, data.

questions.stem: How do Business Intelligence and Business Analytics differ in what they work on?
options: Both work only on real-time data
Business Intelligence forecasts the future; Business Analytics reports the past
Business Intelligence is done on historical data; Business Analytics uses that generated intelligence to predict or forecast future KPIs
Business Intelligence works on unstructured data; Business Analytics on structured data
There is no difference in how they process data
questions.explanation: Business Intelligence is done on historical data, and Business Analytics uses that generated intelligence to predict or forecast the potential KPIs for the future.

questions.stem: Historically, with what was Business Analytics mostly tagged?
options: Automated reporting tools
Database administration
Data warehouse design
Network security
Manual effort by functional, business or financial consultants
questions.explanation: Business Analytics has been around for a long time but was mostly tagged with manual effort by Functional, Business or Financial Consultants.

questions.stem: Why were many companies able to make fortunes from Business Analytics in earlier years?
options: Because business intelligence did not yet exist
Because there were not a lot of tools available in the market for Analytics, so the work was manual
Because governments subsidised analytics
Because data was free to obtain
Because every organisation had its own data scientists
questions.explanation: As there were not many Analytics tools in the market, companies made fortunes for that piece of manual effort.

questions.stem: What enabled customers to become self-sufficient in building in-house data science, machine learning and deep learning models?
options: The retirement of Business Intelligence tools
The end of manual consulting
A drop in the cost of Excel licences
Big Data, NoSQL databases, and tools that can host and process structured, semi-structured and unstructured datasets
New regulations requiring in-house models
questions.explanation: With Big Data, NoSQL databases and tools that can host and process structured, semi-structured and unstructured data, customers became self-sufficient to build their own models.

questions.stem: In the new era, what is the role of Business Intelligence in relation to Business Analytics?
options: Business Intelligence is an input for Business Analytics
Business Intelligence has replaced Business Analytics
Business Intelligence is the output of Business Analytics
Business Intelligence is no longer used
Business Intelligence is only used by consultants
questions.explanation: The new era has brought Business Analytics to the front end, with Business Intelligence now serving as an input for it.

questions.stem: What can business users now plan within their own organisations, saving millions of dollars?
options: Database indexes versus storage costs
Server uptime versus network bandwidth
Use cases versus ROI versus time to market
Hiring versus firing decisions
Printer ink versus paper orders
questions.explanation: Business users can now plan their use cases against ROI and time to market within their own organisations, saving millions of dollars.

questions.stem: What is the consequence of ignoring the importance of Data Strategy while building in-house analytics?
options: A faster time to market
A larger data warehouse
Better customer segmentation
A return to manual consulting
A Data Swamp, with a 180-degree impact on ROI
questions.explanation: Customers should not ignore Data Strategy, or they will face a Data Swamp which will impact their ROI by 180 degrees.

questions.stem: Which statement about Business Intelligence and Business Analytics is NOT correct?
options: Business Intelligence has existed for decades in terms of tools and technologies
Business Intelligence and Business Analytics have the same standing in decision making
Business Analytics predicts or forecasts future KPIs
Organisations used to extract data and hand it to analytics companies
Business Intelligence is done on historical data
questions.explanation: Although they look the same, Business Intelligence and Business Analytics have different standing in terms of decision making.
